chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sa'id ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

For the mudihah, there are five camels; for the simhaq, which is less than the mudihah, there are four camels; for the munaqqilah, there are fifteen camels; for the ja'ifah, there is one-third of the diyah, thirty-three camels; and for the ma'mumah, there is one-third of the diyah.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation due for bodily injury or wrongful harm
key_terms.السِّمْحَاقِ: a wound less severe than the mudihah, with compensation set at four camels
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, the unit in which the compensation is quantified here
key_terms.الْجَائِفَةِ: a penetrating wound reaching an internal cavity, for which one-third of the diyah is due
key_terms.الْمَأْمُومَةِ: a head wound reaching the membrane of the brain, with compensation of one-third of the diyah
key_terms.الْمُنَقِّلَةِ: an injury that displaces or moves the bone, with compensation of fifteen camels
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَةِ: a wound that exposes the bone, for which the compensation is five camels

ai.seo_question: What are the prescribed diyah amounts for different types of head and body wounds in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states specific legal compensations for different categories of wounds and injuries. It is part of the jurisprudence of diyat, assigning measured liability according to the severity and type of bodily harm.
